g.text: Identity & secrets — GET /auth/me → local_user() resolution → the dependency that can never 401,
plus the SEPARATE Salesforce credential ladder and the dead AWS branch
TRUST BOUNDARY — the ONLY one that exists.
Anything that can open a TCP connection to the published port is already 'the owner'.
docker-compose.yml:272-273 publishes 8080:8080 on 0.0.0.0 with no host-IP bind.
A · "Who am I?" — the only identity call in the system
non-ok mapped to 502, bare `catch`. It does not use `lib/proxy.ts`,
whose docstring wrongly claims it serves `/api/auth/*` (proxy.ts:1-2).
[`_cached_user_id` is already set — the normal case]
docker-compose.yml — the one env var that bypasses the config layer.
cheap: it re-runs `executescript(_SCHEMA)` + `migrate()` incl. a full-table
any more, and storing a real one would imply it does (auth.py:74-76).
`sqlite3.IntegrityError` is swallowed as a create race (auth.py:80-81);
`_cached_user_id` is a module-level mutable global read-modify-written
event loop (`async def chat`, main.py:327). Two threads can both miss
and both call `create_user` — which is why :80 swallows `IntegrityError`.
B · require_user() — the dependency that can never fail
`return current_user(request)` and its own docstring says
(auth.py:95-97). There is no cookie, no bearer token, no session, no CSRF
token, no origin check beyond CORS, and no rate limit anywhere.
Routes that DECLARE Depends(require_user) — the dependency always resolves
Routes with NO auth dependency at all
`current_user` is still called at main.py:327 — but only for personalisation
and the conversation-ownership compare, which is itself skipped whenever
`conv_owner is None` and is wrapped in `except Exception: conv_owner = None`
identity to itself and these three routes are open to anything on the port.
• Every `signed_in is None` / `user is None` branch in main.py
the `HTTPException(401)` at main.py:757 can never fire.
direct HTTP client is unaffected; `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=*` is accepted verbatim
installed and unused; main.py:46 still comments about the `ts_session` cookie.
C · Salesforce credentials — a SEPARATE ladder, unrelated to the identity above
C1 · orchestrator live SOQL — client-credentials ONLY (core/salesforce.py:111-141)
in the sync-worker and was not duplicated (core/salesforce.py:119-120).
• `_token` is shared mutable module state with
misses both POST and both write; last write wins, doubling OAuth sessions.
• A fresh `httpx.AsyncClient` per call — no pooling (:123, :148, :157, :180).
`ReadTimeout` escapes as an httpx exception, not `SalesforceUnavailable`,
and `agent.py:295` catches only the latter — a blip aborts the step chain.
• Only one 401 re-auth retry (:154-162). No rate limit, no circuit breaker,
no per-user quota. The response body is never echoed (:132-134) — correct.
no key material is loaded or validated at all
a secret and a key silently ignores the key
when `SF_PRIVATE_KEY_HOST_FILE` is set; :328 bind-mounts the host
, defaulting to `/dev/null` so compose still parses.
even when a caller passes an explicit `env` dict
is why tests must monkeypatch it. Worse, it places the RSA signing key inside
, which docker-compose.yml:269 also mounts into the
orchestrator container that executes LLM-generated SQL.
Secret hygiene here is genuinely good.
(secrets.py:92-95), asserted by tests; no exception message embeds a value;
`.env`, `.env.bak-*` and `secrets/` are gitignored and `git ls-files` shows
`login_url` is never validated as https or well-formed (secrets.py:155-158):
a typo'd `SF_LOGIN_URL` becomes both the JWT `aud` claim and the POST target,
C3 · DEAD PATH — AWS Secrets Manager, removed 2026-07-28
• `sync-worker/syncworker/secrets.py:1-6` documents the removal; there is no
cloud call anywhere in the module.
arguments (secrets.py:172); no live caller passes them.
(2026-07-28) — nothing here calls a cloud service."
But it is still advertised — documentation drift,
and the reason this dead branch is drawn at all:
"used ONLY to read the Salesforce secret from AWS Secrets Manager"
An operator following `.env.example` will populate cloud credentials that
nothing reads — real credentials on disk with no consumer.
the ONLY trust boundary — nothing authenticates across it
code path that no longer exists but is still documented
behaviour that IS implemented, incl. controls that work
risk: no authz, leaked connection, unlocked global, doc drift
